title: Looking back: the sources
hook: Avot, Berakhot, the laws of return, the midrash
tomorrow: Noa owes one teacher a thank-you. which one, and why?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Hillel on one foot and a sign above Owen's sink: two voices, shared ground. The ideas stay. Today closes the week of looking back.

A photo that looks wrong on the screen until you rotate it, and then suddenly it's a face. Some things only make sense from the next angle. Noa's last Shabbat at home, the table crowded, Saba David at the end of it. Someone asks what she's packing besides clothes, and Saba answers for her with a line from Pirkei Avot, the text the two of them have been reading by phone all summer. A sage called Ben Bag Bag said of the Torah: turn it, and turn it again, for everything is in it.
screen: `ROTATE IT, AND IT'S A FACE.` → `THE LAST SHABBAT AT HOME.` → `TURN IT, AND TURN IT AGAIN.`

segments.voice: That's how this path has read its sources: turning them. Avot, the sayings of the sages, short enough to carry in a pocket. Berakhot, the tractate of blessings, which begins with a simple question: from what time may the evening Shema be said? The laws of return, Maimonides' map of teshuvah, of turning back. And the midrash, the rabbis' stories that fill the gaps between the verses. None of them gets used up. You turn them, and another face appears. Every year of this path you've opened them again, and each time they showed you something you'd walked right past. Now turn this week once more. Moses on Nebo, shown the whole land: see it all. A child's question about rules, answered with a story: the stories stay. Hillel's candles, one more each night: the practices stay. A scroll kissed by way of a fringe: the torah stays. A grandfather's voice on a recording: the story stays. A sign above a sink, and Hillel on one foot: the ideas stay. Six turns, and the same Torah underneath.
screen: `TURN IT, AND TURN IT AGAIN.` · `AVOT, BERAKHOT, RETURN, MIDRASH.` · `SIX TURNS THIS WEEK.` · then, large: `THE SOURCES STAY.`

segments.voice: Count the week on your fingers, one line per finger: see it all, the stories stay, the practices stay, the torah stays, the story stays, the ideas stay. When you reach the last, hold that hand still. Then bring back one saying from these years, any one, and say it quietly, turning it once in your mind.
screen: `ONE LINE PER FINGER.` · `HOLD THE HAND STILL.` · `ONE SAYING, TURNED ONCE.`

segments.voice: Looking back: the sources. Avot, Berakhot, the laws of return and the midrash, turned and turned again.
The week's line: the sources stay, and there's always another side to turn. Eight of fourteen, and Shabbat shalom.

screen: `DAY 1785 COUNTS.` → `THE SUMMIT · 8 OF 14.` → `TOMORROW: NOA OWES ONE TEACHER A THANK-YOU. WHICH ONE?`
